learningObjectives.title: Magnetic fields, field lines & plotting compass
Electromagnetism — field around a wire & solenoid
Motor effect — F=BIL & Fleming's left hand

questions.q: Two magnets are placed near each other. Which pairing will REPEL?
options: North pole near south pole
South pole near north pole
North pole near north pole
A magnet near an unmagnetised iron nail
questions.explain: Like poles repel, so two north poles push apart. Unlike poles (N–S) attract, and an unmagnetised iron nail is always attracted (induced magnetism).

questions.q: In what direction do magnetic field lines around a bar magnet point?
options: From south pole to north pole outside the magnet
From north pole to south pole outside the magnet
Always towards the nearest pole
In random directions
questions.explain: By convention, magnetic field lines travel from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet. The direction is the direction of the force on a north pole.

questions.q: What is the shape of the magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire?
options: Straight lines along the wire
Concentric circles around the wire
A field like a bar magnet
No field is produced
questions.explain: A current in a straight wire produces a magnetic field of concentric circles around the wire. The field is stronger nearer the wire and with a larger current.

questions.q: The motor effect produces the LARGEST force on a current-carrying wire when the wire is...
options: Parallel to the magnetic field
At 45° to the magnetic field
At 90° (perpendicular) to the magnetic field
Outside any magnetic field
questions.explain: The force is greatest when the wire is perpendicular (90°) to the field. When the wire is parallel to the field, the force is zero.

questions.q: Which action will induce a potential difference in a coil of wire? (generator effect)
options: Holding a stationary magnet inside the coil
Moving a magnet into or out of the coil
Placing the coil far from any magnet
Leaving the coil in a steady magnetic field
questions.explain: A potential difference is induced only when there is a change in the magnetic field through the coil, e.g. moving a magnet in or out. A stationary magnet causes no induced p.d.

questions.q: A step-up transformer has more turns on the secondary coil than the primary. What does it do to the potential difference?
options: Decreases the p.d.
Increases the p.d.
Leaves the p.d. unchanged
Converts ac to dc
questions.explain: In a step-up transformer np < ns, so by Vp/Vs = np/ns the secondary (output) p.d. is greater than the primary. The current is correspondingly smaller.

questions.q: Which statement about permanent and induced magnets is correct?
options: An induced magnet always repels a permanent magnet
An induced magnet only becomes magnetic in a magnetic field and quickly loses it when removed
A permanent magnet loses its magnetism as soon as it is moved away from iron
Induced magnetism produces a force of repulsion
questions.explain: Induced magnetism appears only while a material is in a magnetic field and is lost (or much reduced) when removed. Induced magnets always cause attraction, never repulsion.

questions.q: Where is the magnetic field of a bar magnet STRONGEST?
options: At the centre of the magnet
Where the field lines are most spread out
At the poles, where the field lines are closest together
Everywhere the field strength is the same
questions.explain: The closer together the field lines, the stronger the field. Lines are most concentrated at the poles, so the field is strongest there.

questions.q: Which change would NOT increase the strength of an electromagnet (solenoid)?
options: Increasing the current
Adding more turns of wire
Adding an iron core
Using a thicker plastic former with no iron
questions.explain: Electromagnet strength increases with more current, more turns and an iron core. A plastic former with no iron does not boost the field.

questions.q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, what does the THUMB represent?
options: The magnetic field
The current
The direction of the force (motion)
The voltage
questions.explain: Fleming's left-hand rule: First finger = Field, seCond finger = Current, thuMb = Motion (force). It gives the direction of the force on the conductor.

questions.q: What is the key difference between an alternator and a dynamo?
options: An alternator produces direct current (dc); a dynamo produces alternating current (ac)
An alternator uses slip rings and produces ac; a dynamo uses a split-ring commutator and produces dc
They are identical in every way
A dynamo uses no magnets
questions.explain: An alternator uses slip rings, giving alternating current (ac). A dynamo uses a split-ring commutator, which reverses the connections each half turn to give direct current (dc).

questions.q: A transformer has 100 turns on the primary and 500 turns on the secondary. The primary p.d. is 12 V. Calculate the secondary p.d.
questions.explain: Vp/Vs = np/ns, so Vs = Vp × ns/np = 12 × 500/100 = 60 V. This is a step-up transformer.

questions.q: Which material would make the BEST permanent magnet?
options: Steel
Pure soft iron
Copper
Aluminium
questions.explain: Steel is magnetically hard and retains its magnetism, making good permanent magnets. Soft iron is easily magnetised but loses it quickly (good for electromagnet cores), while copper and aluminium are non-magnetic.

questions.q: What is the best tool for plotting the shape and direction of a magnetic field around a bar magnet?
options: A voltmeter
A plotting (small) compass
An ammeter
A thermometer
questions.explain: A plotting compass needle aligns with the field at each point, letting you trace the field lines and their direction. Iron filings show the shape but not the direction.

questions.q: Why is the field of a solenoid similar to that of a bar magnet?
options: Because the wire is made of iron
Because the fields from each loop add up to give a strong uniform field inside and a bar-magnet field outside
Because solenoids contain permanent magnets
Because the current flows in a circle only once
questions.explain: The circular fields from each turn combine to give a strong, nearly uniform field inside the solenoid and an external field shaped like that of a bar magnet, with a north and south end.

questions.q: How can you reverse the direction of the force on a wire in an electric motor?
options: Only by switching off the current
By reversing either the current OR the magnetic field direction
By increasing the current
It is impossible to reverse the force
questions.explain: Reversing the current direction or the magnetic field direction reverses the force. (Reversing both at once returns the force to its original direction.)

questions.q: How can you increase the size of the induced potential difference from a generator?
options: Move the magnet or coil more slowly
Use fewer turns on the coil
Move the magnet faster, use more turns, or use a stronger magnet
Keep the magnet stationary
questions.explain: A larger induced p.d. results from a faster rate of change of the field, more turns on the coil, or a stronger magnet — all increase how quickly field lines are cut.

questions.q: A transformer has 800 turns on the primary and 200 turns on the secondary. The primary p.d. is 230 V. Calculate the secondary p.d.
questions.explain: Vp/Vs = np/ns, so Vs = Vp × ns/np = 230 × 200/800 = 57.5 V. This is a step-down transformer.

questions.q: A compass needle always points roughly north. What does this tell us?
options: The Earth has no magnetic field
The Earth has a magnetic field, evidence its core is magnetic
Compasses are attracted to the Sun
Magnetic fields do not affect compasses
questions.explain: A compass needle is a tiny magnet that aligns with the Earth's magnetic field, providing evidence that the Earth's core is magnetic.

questions.q: A wire of length 0.20 m carries a current of 3.0 A at right angles to a magnetic field of 0.50 T. Calculate the force on the wire.
questions.explain: F = BIL = 0.50 × 3.0 × 0.20 = 0.30 N. The wire is perpendicular to the field, so the full force formula applies.

questions.q: A 100% efficient transformer has a primary p.d. of 230 V and primary current of 2.0 A. The secondary p.d. is 23 V. Calculate the secondary current.
questions.explain: For an ideal transformer VpIp = VsIs, so Is = VpIp/Vs = (230 × 2.0)/23 = 460/23 = 20 A.

questions.q: A 0.40 m wire experiences a force of 0.60 N when carrying a current of 5.0 A perpendicular to a magnetic field. Calculate the magnetic flux density.
Why does the national grid use step-up transformers before transmission over long distances?
options: To increase the current and reduce the voltage
To increase the voltage and reduce the current, which reduces energy lost as heat in the cables
To convert ac to dc for transmission
To make the cables thicker
questions.explain: Stepping up the p.d. reduces the current for the same power (P = VI). Lower current means much less energy wasted as heat in the resistance of the transmission cables (heating ∝ I²R).
